title: Quantum State Routing and Perfect State Transfer on Signed Graphs under Environmental Noise
abstract: Routing unknown quantum information across distributed communication networks requires autonomous, measurement-free mechanisms to prevent wave-function collapse. Szegedy quantum walks provide a mechanism for spatial state transport. The conventional walks on unweighted graphs suffer from severe back-reflection, spatial dispersion, and channel crosstalk. In this paper, we introduce a deterministic topological quantum routing architecture based on coined Szegedy quantum walks on edge-duplicated signed graphs. By treating edge signs as localized phase shifts within a balanced coin reflection, we enforce an exact zero back-scattering condition across routing nodes. We demonstrate deterministic Perfect State Transfer (PST) with unit fidelity at exact arrival times across fundamental archetypes, including the signed dumbbell switch $D_{2m,0,2n}$ and scalable glued binary trees. Furthermore, we analyse routing performance under realistic open-system amplitude and phase damping noise channels.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, measurement-free quantum routing architecture using coined quantum walks on signed graphs. By engineering the graph structure with controlled phase shifts, the authors achieve deterministic Perfect State Transfer (PST) and demonstrate that the protocol maintains high fidelity over significant distances even when subjected to realistic amplitude and phase damping noise.
main_problem: The core problem is achieving measurement-free, deterministic routing of unknown quantum information across distributed networks while mitigating decoherence from environmental noise.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that using coined quantum walks on signed graphs enables Perfect State Transfer (PST) with unit fidelity, and they derive analytical limits showing the protocol's resilience against amplitude and phase damping noise.
method: The research employs the formalism of coined Szegedy quantum walks on specially constructed signed graphs, treating edge signs as localized $\pi$-phase shifts to enforce destructive interference and zero back-scattering.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum router modeled by coined quantum walks on edge-duplicated signed graphs ($\vec{\Sigma}$). Positive edges are standard waveguides, while negative edges introduce controlled $\pi$-phase shifts, enabling topological control over state propagation.
key_observables: Fidelity ($F$), Back-scattering suppression, Maximum achievable hop distance ($	au_{\max}$) under noise.
important_parameters: Control parameter $\alpha=0.5$, Amplitude damping rate ($\lambda$), Phase damping rate ($p$), Graph topology (e.g., dumbbell switch $D_{2m,0,2n}$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes the physical feasibility of implementing localized $\pi$-phase shifts using external modulators, and the noise analysis assumes noise acts independently at each discrete time step.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the signed graph structure, the process of generating the signed directed graph from an undirected one, and examples of the topological archetypes used for routing.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for measurement-free routing, critiques conventional quantum walks, introduces the signed graph model to enforce zero back-scattering, proves deterministic PST on archetypes, and concludes with a detailed analysis of noise robustness.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum network communication, which is a major focus area for quantum information theorists. The use of topological invariants (edge signs) to achieve robustness against noise is highly relevant to building fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
